real_conflicts: The proposal to introduce 'subtle background tints' to the three headline cards (variety_distinctiveness) threatens the strict color discipline of the design. The current system uses a neutral cream background to let the data accents (red, teal, blue) pop; adding tinted backgrounds creates a 'muddy' visual noise that breaks the clean editorial rhythm and makes the palette feel arbitrary rather than systematic.
accepted: Extending the rainfall chart's x-axis to include 'Nov' (completeness_density) is essential for rhythmic consistency. The temperature and rainfall charts must share the exact same temporal grid to maintain the visual logic of the 'editorial narrative.'

Moving the 'HIGH FLOOD RISK WINDOW' label to avoid overlapping the data bars (simplicity_legibility) aligns with the mandate for consistent typography and clear data encoding. The current placement is a visual error that breaks the grid.
concession: I concede that the 'High Flood Risk Window' label needs to be moved to the empty space above the bars, but I reject the idea of changing its color to a neutral dark. It must remain red to maintain the semantic link to the 'High Risk' red used in the temperature chart and the 'High-Risk Districts' markers. The color is the rule; the position was the error.
compromise: We will extend the rainfall chart to 12 months to match the temperature chart's rhythm. We will move the 'High Flood Risk Window' label to the top-left of the pink shaded zone (above the bars) and keep it red, but increase the letter-spacing to match the 'TEMPERATURE INCREASE' header style. We will reject the background tints on the cards to preserve the unified white-card system.
nonnegotiable: The three headline indicator cards must remain on a uniform white background to preserve the 'system' feel of the infographic; they are the structural anchors, not decorative elements.
